summary: Clearwater NF ground site on Grave Butte: 1928 tent camp, 1929 log cupola cabin, last manned 1940, buildings condemned 1954; no source describes what remains today.

facts.design: Log cupola cabin with L-3 lookout cab, with shake-covered woodshed, root cellar and outhouse added later
facts.status_note: Buildings condemned 1954; Hartig (1981) then says Bill O'Brien went in to do the torch job, with no detail on the outcome; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Idaho list marks the site Gone; no source describes the site today

staffing.status: Ranger-staffed from a 1928 tent camp, then the 1929-30 cabin; last manned 1940 per Hartig (1981)

visit.trail_note: Hike-in site per Idaho Fire Lookouts; no trail or permission details in the sources read

events.note: Ranger Ralph Hand set up a tent camp on the south side of the peak as a seasonal detection point
Log cupola cabin with L-3 lookout cab; construction began 1929. The Clearwater list's year column reads 1928 for the camp row; see resolved_conflicts
Bald Mountain fire threatened the unfinished cabin; crew dug a trench and burned out the area inside it
Earnest Hartman and Harry Chenoweth sent to finish the cabin that summer, under Ranger Fred Shaner
Buildings condemned; a packer salvaged usable items; Bill O'Brien then went in to do the torch job (what it destroyed is not described; year not given)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Clearwater list's year column reads 1928 for the camp row, and its notes give '1929-log cupola' for the cabin. Hartig (1981) says the butte was first used in 1928 as a tent camp and that cabin construction began in 1929. The story gives 1928 for first use and 1929 for the cabin.
Firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Clearwater list give the 1950s for abandonment. Hartig says the last manning was 1940 and the buildings were condemned in 1954. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: Idaho County, Clearwater NF, 6,190 ft, ground type and gone all match. The brief had no design; L-3 comes from Hartig (1981) via Forest Lookouts. The access level is omitted because sources say hike-in but describe no permissions. Nothing in the sources describes the site today. Hartig's 'torch job' is quoted without detail; the story says only that Bill O'Brien went in to do it, and Hartig is the only source for the fate of the buildings.
